items.title: Extract a provenance-checked cloud-worker case set
items.instructions: Create `bench/worker_eval/build_cases.py`, `bench/worker_eval/cases.jsonl`, and document the schema in `bench/worker_eval/README.md`. The builder runs on the host and reads `~/Projects/bonsai-garden/autopilot/.runtime/calls/`, the `auto/M1-ngram` journal, and git history without modifying anything under `autopilot/`. Select at least 20 successful cloud-worker rounds at or after 2026-10-12 08:33, excluding rate-limited `spec-replay` rounds and any round without a recoverable request. Include at least two plan items and do not exclude `revise` verdicts. Each JSONL row must contain a stable case ID, milestone/item/round, source timestamp and model, the `autopilot(<m>): before <item> round <n>` start commit, the exact first user prompt with only its worker-description text changed to the canonical Bonsai replay description, the cloud request including its source (tool or JSON fallback), and the following advisor verdict and notes. Preserve source prompt and event-log hashes or equivalent provenance so the substitution can be audited. Add validation that commits exist, prompts and requests are nonempty, the model substitution occurs exactly once, verdicts align chronologically with their requests, IDs are unique, and the coverage/count rules hold.
items.acceptance: `bench/worker_eval/cases.jsonl` has at least 20 valid rows from the required time range and at least two distinct `item` values; a committed inventory reports counts by source model, item, request kind, and advisor verdict. Every referenced start commit resolves and has the expected before-round subject. Re-running `python3 bench/worker_eval/build_cases.py --check` on the host exits 0 without changing the file, reports no included rate-limit failures, and demonstrates that each stored prompt differs from its recorded first user message only in the single worker-description substitution. At least one `revise` case is retained if any eligible source round received that verdict.

items.title: Define worker arms and implement the resumable replay harness
items.instructions: Add a documented arm schema under `bench/worker_eval/arms/` with fields for model, worker description, thinking level, maximum output tokens, compaction reserve, session timeout, worker memory, and extra extensions. Add `bonsai-2026-10-12.json`, deriving every setting from the historical config/model registration rather than guessing: reproduce the 2026-10-12 Bonsai worker, except set memory off and timeout to 20 minutes; load `submit_request.ts` as an extra extension. Implement `bench/worker_eval/run.py ARM [--cases PATH] [--repeat N]` using the existing eval sandbox/tap helpers read-only. For each `(arm, case, repeat)`, create a fresh detached checkout of the case's start commit under `/tmp`, outside the milestone worktree; create a fresh pi agent directory; render and verify the replay-model line; run with no sandbox network through the tap to live `bonsai-agent` using the bench key; and remove the checkout afterward. Never edit `autopilot/` or live configuration. Support a stable `--out` directory and a chunk budget (default no more than 145 minutes): do not launch a case unless its 20-minute timeout fits in the remaining budget. Resume by skipping only completed unique `(arm, case_id, repeat)` records. Save a manifest, event stream, final text, request, and workspace diff for each attempt. Detect requests from `request.json` first, otherwise the last JSON object in the final reply, otherwise none; apply the submit-request field rules and the orchestrator's per-kind path/command checks against that replay checkout. Record request source and body, validation errors, valid-request boolean, cloud/replay kinds and kind-match boolean, wall seconds, turns, tool calls by tool, tool errors by tool, compaction start/end counts, every assistant stop reason and the last one, raw error messages, and explicit timeout/context-overflow/output-limit flags. Add fixture-based tests for event parsing, JSON fallback, validation, error classification, model substitution, and resume behavior.
items.acceptance: `bench/worker_eval/arms/schema.json`, `bench/worker_eval/arms/bonsai-2026-10-12.json`, `bench/worker_eval/run.py`, and tests exist. The baseline arm explicitly has memory disabled, a 20-minute timeout, a 28,672-token compaction reserve, the historical 16,384-token output cap unless the provenance proves otherwise, and the historical thinking level, with sources cited in `README.md`. Tests pass locally without GPU or network. A host smoke run of one case completes through the live turnstile bench route with `gpu=false`, leaves the milestone worktree unchanged except for results, creates its checkout outside that worktree, produces all required fields and artifacts, and a second invocation skips the completed attempt without duplicating its result. The manifest pins the repository commit, cases and arm hashes, pi version, model registration, and non-secret live routing/server metadata.

items.title: Run Bonsai at N=2 and summarize deterministic outcomes
items.instructions: Run `bonsai-2026-10-12` on every case with two repeats, using repeated resumable host requests of at most 150 minutes each and one fixed dated output directory under `bench/results/<date>/worker-eval/bonsai-2026-10-12/`. These use the live turnstile bench key, so request them with `gpu=false`; do not start a private server or alter the live stack. Add `bench/worker_eval/summarize.py` to verify completeness and write `summary.json` plus `summary.md`. Report per case and pooled: attempts, valid requests and rate, kind matches and rate over all attempts, kind matches conditional on valid requests, median wall time, median turns, tool-call totals/by-tool, tool-error totals/by-tool, compactions, last-stop-reason counts, and timeout/context-overflow/output-limit flags. Include a failure table for every invalid or absent request. Treat the failure flags as potentially overlapping and state their denominators; also identify unclassified no-request and invalid-request failures rather than forcing them into a known category.
items.acceptance: The dated result directory contains exactly two completed records for every case and no duplicate `(case_id, repeat)` keys; its manifest proves use of `bonsai-2026-10-12` and the bench-key live route. `summarize.py --check <result-dir>` exits 0 and recomputes all reported values from `results.jsonl`. `summary.json` and `summary.md` contain the required per-case and pooled valid-request rates, both kind-match denominators, median times, and failure-mode counts. Every timeout, context overflow, and output-limit count traces to an attempt's explicit flag and raw event/error evidence, and every case is represented even when both repeats failed.

items.title: Grade a deterministic sample of valid Bonsai requests
items.instructions: Select at most 10 replay attempts whose requests passed deterministic checks, using a documented deterministic rule such as request-kind stratification followed by SHA-256 ordering of run IDs; do not hand-pick good-looking outputs. Prefer kinds the real orchestrator sends to review (`run`, `infra`, and `done`) and state any exclusions. Build a grading packet for each selection from `autopilot/prompts/review.md`, the original case milestone/item context, the Bonsai request, its replay-worktree diff and preserved requested files, and the corresponding kind-specific review instruction from `autopilot.py`. Use the autopilot advisor review gate to obtain an independent `approve`, `revise`, or `reject` for each request: on the first finished-item review ask the advisor to return all per-attempt grades, then persist that response verbatim and resubmit for transcription verification. Do not infer grades from deterministic request validity and do not include the original cloud worker's verdict as the Bonsai grade.
items.acceptance: The result directory contains the sample manifest, filled grading packets or their hashes, `advisor_grades.jsonl`, and `advisor_summary.md`. There are 1–10 unique sampled attempts, all marked deterministically valid in `results.jsonl`, and the selection can be regenerated exactly. Every grade names the advisor model, run ID, request kind, verdict, and rationale and is traceable to an advisor journal response using `autopilot/prompts/review.md`. The summary reports approval/revision/rejection counts and approval rate with its sample denominator, separately from valid-request and kind-match rates, and clearly labels this as a small judged sample.

items.title: Publish the W1 experiment and update parent summaries
items.instructions: Following `site/AUTHORING.md`, create the local-worker series page at `site/series/local-worker/index.md` and the W1 experiment page at `site/series/local-worker/worker-eval.md`; update `site/index.md` as the project parent. The experiment must state the question, corpus construction and exclusions, exact arm, N=2 run size, deterministic pooled and per-case results, failure-mode breakdown with denominators, and the separately sampled advisor grades. Link claims to the committed case set and dated result artifacts. Discuss what observed failures point to for W2—thinking/history retention and output budget, tool-output caps, editing/tool errors, session discipline, and compaction—but distinguish measured evidence from hypotheses. Update `README.md` and `docs/roadmap.md` so W1's status and next step agree with the site; do not claim Bonsai can or cannot replace the cloud worker beyond what the rates and sample support.
items.acceptance: `site/series/local-worker/worker-eval.md` has valid experiment front matter, a summary of at most 200 words, exact numbers matching `summary.json` and `advisor_grades.jsonl`, per-case and pooled tables, explicit caveats, and evidence-linked W2 priorities. `site/series/local-worker/index.md` and `site/index.md` have current hand-written summaries and `updated` dates no older than the experiment. `README.md` and `docs/roadmap.md` consistently record W1's result and W2 as the next local-worker step. `python3 tools/check_site.py` passes, and the final advisor review verifies every numerical claim against committed result files.
